summary: Implemented versioned, fail-closed component runtime conformance. Production verification now requires every complete component contract to map to current runtime-tree source files, exact data-component DOM markers, hashed and fresh state/interaction/responsive scenario evidence, and explicit contract coverage. Static HTML fixtures, tamper cases, runtime changes, and the non-production-only v0 legacy boundary are covered by tests and documentation.
decisions: Use component-runtime-manifest/v1 and component-runtime-evidence/v1 as explicit production schemas; an absent manifest or component-runtime-manifest/v0 is never production eligible.

Bind every complete contract ID to source files that are both content-hashed and present in the current sha256-runtime-tree-v1 file list, preventing excluded build evidence from impersonating runtime source.

Require exact quoted data-component-id and data-component-part source markers, then bind the same markers into the hashed evidence artifact instead of inferring correspondence from CSS selectors or visual similarity.

Require complete state, event, transition, focus, responsive-width, control-rule, container, prop, data, content, accessibility, variant, provenance, and empty-state coverage before a component is verified.
Keep cli.py unchanged by using the documented project-local default manifest path and an optional verifier API override.
Permit missing or explicit v0 evidence only when a caller opts out of a production claim; such reports remain verified false and production_eligible false.

risks: Existing projects that lack v1 runtime evidence now intentionally fail production verification until UI implementation and production QA generate current evidence.

The validator verifies hashes, freshness, exact markers, and coverage structure; production QA must still confirm that passed assertions were emitted by the recorded browser or component-test run rather than manually authored.
